blocks.text: Quay homes listed and sold, June to September 2026

Quay, September 2026. No detached houses were listed or sold in Quay between June and September. Condos and townhomes: 59 listed at month end and 16 sold in September, a sales ratio of 27% (a sellers’ market).

On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Condos and townhomes: 51 sold over 4 months against an average of 66.8 listed, about 5.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was September with 16 sold.

New Westminster real estate market stats

No fee-simple house lot stock exists in the Quay on the verified record: the City's floodplain study describes the Quay as high-density residential along the Fraser River, and the September 2026 market recorded no detached stock at all. A buyer set on this waterfront is choosing between strata buildings, not between lots.

Lot character from the zones: waterfront parcels sit in multiple-unit residential and comprehensive development districts under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, with zone-specific minimums in the bylaw text; a Quay-specific minimum lot size is UNVERIFIED — no figure is published here.

Serviced position: the waterfront is fully urban strata stock served by City water / sewer and the City's own electrical utility; a 2026 utility dollar figure for a Quay strata unit is UNVERIFIED, and no well/septic position arises on this evidence.

ALR vs non-ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land is identified in the Quay in the sources read; ALR status for a specific property is a per-address check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Flood position — the defining fact: the City's floodplain study places the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3 — the Fraser River waterfront zone — where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level, but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. This is the defining due-diligence item for every Quay purchase.

Market context, labelled correctly: New Westminster IS a SnapStats-covered community. SnapStats has NO land category, and no figure below is a land figure. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).
No bare-land strata plan in the Quay was verified: — the waterfront's strata are conventional apartment stratas (towers, mid-rises and two low-rises), not bare-land plans.

Non-market co-operative land tenure — excluded, with the reason stated: Westminster Landing (13 K de K Court, 84 units) and Riverbend (1050 Quayside Drive, 72 units) are co-operative / non-market complexes in the City's non-market inventory, with units spread across seniors, single, disabled and family columns — membership housing, not strata lots or fee-simple land a buyer can purchase. Excluded from land stock.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Quay

items.t: The Quay is the City of New Westminster's Downtown waterfront neighbourhood along Quayside Drive on the Fraser River; "Quay" is the GVR board sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report, and the City's context-statement name for the same waterfront is "Quayside," listed among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements. Precise board boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.

The working extent is the Fraser River waterfront along Quayside Drive, from Westminster Pier Park east along the Waterfront Esplanade. Nearby areas: Downtown directly above the waterfront, Uptown up the hill, Victoria Hill to the east, and Queensborough across the Fraser River to the south.

Roads and transit: Quayside Drive is the waterfront road; Columbia Street and 8th Street link the Quay to Downtown and New Westminster Station, and Stewardson Way links west toward Marine Way and Burnaby. New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) serve the Quay at the top of the waterfront; TransLink route 103 is the Quayside / New Westminster Station route and route 102 serves Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station. Commute times in minutes are UNVERIFIED.

Waterfront anchors: Westminster Pier Park, 600 Quayside Drive; Quayside Park (with a water play area); and the Waterfront Esplanade boardwalk running the length of the waterfront. A library kiosk and holds locker are at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, at the top of the waterfront; the Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown. Hospital: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Quay

items.t: Floodplain Zone 3 is the defining diligence item for Quay land: the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying zones including the Quay; confirm the specific building's flood construction level compliance and the strata's insurance and deductible position lot by lot before subject removal.
Plan: the Downtown Community Plan (Schedule C of the OCP) governs the downtown waterfront, under "Our City 2041," the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Quay ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm-class thresholds are not documented in this area's own research, so no farm-class figure is asserted here.

The living space is above the flood level; the way out is not (Zone 3's exact trap): the City's floodplain study notes that in Zone 3 many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level, but egress and the waterfront path sit below it — a distinction that shapes strata insurance and emergency planning, and one that listing copy never mentions.

Tiffany Shores is four addresses, one strata: 1210, 1220, 1230 and 1240 Quayside Drive sit under a single strata corporation, NWS2924, managed by Quay Pacific — document orders and depreciation reports run to the corporation, not to the individual street address.

The Quay has two names and both are official in different places: the board sub-area name is "Quay" (SnapStats GVR); the City's heritage context name is "Quayside," and the street, park and bus route all use Quayside. Searches under only one name miss records filed under the other.

Westminster Pier Park, 600 Quayside Drive, is the waterfront's landmark, connecting with Quayside Park (with a water play area) and the Waterfront Esplanade boardwalk that runs the length of the waterfront — the amenity is public and continuous, not a building feature.

faq.q: Is the Quay in the Fraser River floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it; confirm the specific building's compliance and insurance.

faq.q: What sold in the Quay in September 2026?
faq.a: Condos & townhomes: 16 solds from 59 listings, a 27% sales ratio; there was no detached stock listed. At the New Westminster community level the condos & townhomes median sale price was $560,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations and bus serve the Quay?
faq.a: New Westminster Station and Columbia Station, both on the Expo Line, at the top of the waterfront; TransLink route 103 runs between Quayside and New Westminster Station.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Quay address?
faq.a: For the sample address 800 Carnarvon Street, the SD40 locator result is École Qayqayt Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary; catchments are address-based, so check the exact Quayside Drive address in the locator.

faq.q: What park anchors the Quay waterfront?
faq.a: Westminster Pier Park, 600 Quayside Drive, connects with Quayside Park and the Waterfront Esplanade boardwalk along the Fraser River.

faq.q: Can I buy a lot — or a detached house — in the Quay?
faq.a: There is no fee-simple lot inventory here to buy.

faq.q: What does Floodplain Zone 3 mean for a ground-level unit?
faq.a: Confirm the unit's own floor level against the building's FCL compliance, plus the strata insurance position, in the strata documents — not the listing.

faq.q: Are Westminster Landing and Riverbend land I can buy into?
faq.a: No — they are co-operative / non-market complexes (84 and 72 units, mixed tenures) in the City's non-market inventory; membership housing, not strata title or fee-simple land for sale.

faq.q: How active is this market, honestly?
faq.a: Building-by-building pricing beats city-wide averages here, and SnapStats publishes no Quay-specific median.
